title: A fixed pre-1981 rain model did not resolve a larger 1997 runoff step in Victoria than in New South Wales
abstract: Does a 1997 runoff step differ between Victoria and New South Wales (NSW) after daily rain controls? We fitted rain models through 1980 and kept them fixed for 1981-2021. Controls include annual and seasonal rain, prior-year rain, wet-day count, daily concentration and rain in multi-day wet spells. An interrupted trend allows a separate slope on each side of 1997. CAMELS-AUS v2.03 supplies 67 Victorian and 32 NSW catchments. With AGCD rain, the fitted step was -11.5 percentage points of mean training runoff in Victoria and -3.0 in NSW. Their paired difference was -8.5 points, with conditional 95% limits of -38.1 to +9.3. With SILO rain, the difference was -13.8 (-43.3 to +1.6). Both contrast intervals included zero under ridge penalties of 0.1, 1 and 10. The SILO Victorian step alone was negative in all three settings. This test does not resolve distinct regional timing. It does not show equal changes or exclude a drought effect. Limits include only 16 pre-break test years, seven Victorian and six NSW spatial cells, fixed rain fits, changing site coverage, omitted evaporation and no test of other break dates. Code, provenance and aggregate results support reproduction.

display.caption: Fixed pre-1981 rain fits and the 1997 regional step contrast. Bounds are conditional spatial and residual-time block intervals.
Secondary comparison of annual, seasonal and wet-spell rainfall models on common held-out years.
